scope: Talvora Control Center and desktop progress reliability quality pass: notification-side-effect isolation, redacted bounded exception diagnostics, WPF dispatcher resilience, and operational log quality.

libraries.verified: Current ASP.NET Core MCP filter contract: AddCallToolFilter can wrap every CallTool request while preserving the downstream tool result. Ordinary tool failures may be returned as CallToolResult with IsError=true rather than thrown; cancellation/protocol exceptions retain their documented semantics. Talvora therefore detects thrown and returned failures, aggregates concurrent meaningful calls into one user-facing worklog card, and wraps start/progress/terminal notification side effects so observability can never alter, mask, cancel, or replace the underlying tool result.
Current Microsoft.Extensions.AI and Microsoft.Extensions package alignment guidance for .NET 10.

Current .NET disposal guidance: objects that own unmanaged resources/handles must be deterministically disposed; Process objects are disposable and even temporary Process allocation has handle/lifetime cost. Talvora therefore disposes every Process returned by GetProcesses/GetProcessesByName probes, avoids invariant per-request process/service detection, and retains current NuGet Central Package Management, lock/locked restore, audit, and SDK pinning contracts.

Current WPF-UI Snackbar guidance confirms presenter-owned nonmodal notification UX with explicit timeout; Talvora keeps the existing WPF-UI design language while using a tray-owned WPF progress card so full text, coalescing, hover pause and lifecycle remain under Talvora control.

Current WPF dispatcher guidance confirms UI callbacks execute through Dispatcher operations and DispatcherTimer participates in the same UI lifetime. Talvora keeps known-valid positive timer intervals, preserves direct DragMove/pinned positioning, and isolates desktop-progress presentation failures inside the notification presenter so a non-critical observability surface cannot terminate the Tray/Control Center process.
